assessments.strategy: Oligonucleotides cannot themselves force ribosomal readthrough. The only coherent oligonucleotide contribution is adjuvant: raise mutant DMD transcript abundance by blunting nonsense-mediated decay so a readthrough agent (ataluren-class small molecule, or an engineered suppressor tRNA, which is an RNA not an oligo modality) has more template. Two sub-strategies: (a) sequence-specific NMD evasion using a steric-block ASO over the exon 55 PTC region / downstream exon-junction-complex deposition site, which is largely conceptual in DMD; (b) systemic ASO knockdown of UPF1/SMG1, which is non-selective and raises genome-wide NMD-substrate burden. Neither is a credible standalone therapy; (a) is at best a tool compound to measure whether template abundance is the limiting variable.

delivery_feasibility.target_tissue: Skeletal muscle (whole body, ~40% of body mass) and heart; secondarily CNS
delivery_feasibility.target_cell: Post-mitotic multinucleated myofibers and cardiomyocytes — nuclear compartment
delivery_feasibility.expected_access: Poor for naked chemistry. Systemically dosed PMO/2'-MOE reaches myofiber nuclei at low single-digit-percent efficiency and cardiomyocytes essentially not at all; this is the historical ceiling of the approved DMD exon-skipping drugs. Conjugate chemistries (peptide-PMO, antibody-oligonucleotide) are the only routes with a plausible path to heart and to therapeutic myofiber fractions, and both are early: PGN-EDO51 (peptide-conjugated) was voluntarily discontinued by its sponsor (NCT06079736 TERMINATED, NCT06833931 WITHDRAWN), while BMN 351 (NCT06280209, NCT07573631) and WVE-N531 (NCT04906460, NCT07209332) remain active. (EVIDENCE, ClinicalTrials.gov)
delivery_feasibility.major_constraint: For this hypothesis the constraint is conceptual before it is pharmacokinetic: an NMD-modulating ASO does not restore dystrophin on its own, so it can only be a potentiator whose benefit is gated by a separate readthrough agent.

supporting_evidence.statement: Human proof that readthrough can generate dystrophin protein in nonsense DMD exists (ataluren Phase 2a biopsy study), establishing that template-limitation is a meaningful variable worth measuring.
Multiple oligonucleotide programs have reached clinic in DMD and been dosed repeatedly in children, so chronic systemic oligonucleotide dosing in this population is procedurally established.
If NMD is the limiting factor for this exon 55 PTC, a steric-block ASO tiled across the PTC/downstream EJC region could raise mutant transcript abundance and act as a readthrough potentiator.

contradictory_evidence.statement: No oligonucleotide agent of any maturity targets translation termination; readthrough is mechanistically a ribosome/release-factor event that steric-block or RNase-H chemistry cannot execute. This hypothesis names the wrong modality.

Systemic NMD suppression (UPF1/SMG1 knockdown) stabilizes thousands of physiological NMD substrates; no NMD-inhibitor oligonucleotide has entered clinical development for any indication, and the therapeutic index is unknown.
Suvodirsen (WVE-210201) failed a Phase 2/3 for lack of efficacy, showing that reaching the myofiber nucleus with a stereopure DMD oligonucleotide at clinically meaningful levels is not solved.

assessments.biggest_unknown: Whether the exon 55 mutant transcript is actually NMD-limited. If patient myotubes show near-normal DMD mRNA, an NMD-modulating oligonucleotide has no job at all and the whole oligonucleotide contribution to this hypothesis collapses.
assessments.biggest_failure_mode: Modality mismatch: the oligonucleotide can at most increase template, not increase readthrough, so if readthrough efficiency at this codon context is the binding constraint the ASO adds nothing while adding full systemic toxicity and renal/hepatic exposure risk.
assessments.conclusion_note: No oligonucleotide agent — approved, clinical or validated tool — addresses PTC readthrough or targeted NMD evasion in DMD. Oligonucleotides are the wrong modality for this hypothesis; the honest recommendation is to pursue it as small molecule (ataluren-class) or RNA (anticodon-engineered tRNA), and to use an NMD-blocking ASO only as a bench reagent to answer the template-abundance question.

assessments.strategy: This is a genuine oligonucleotide hypothesis and the only frame-restoring route for an exon 55 PTC that does not require editing. Deliver a cocktail of ~10-11 steric-block ASOs (PMO or 2'-MOE/PS, ideally peptide-conjugated) targeting the splice enhancers and 3' splice sites of exons 45 through 55, so that the spliceosome bridges from exon 44 to exon 56, producing an in-frame internally deleted Dp427m retaining the N-terminal actin-binding and cysteine-rich/C-terminal domains. Critical preparatory step: before committing to the 11-exon geometry, compute from the patient's own transcript whether a smaller frame-neutral block containing exon 55 exists (candidate windows are considerably cheaper pharmacologically and should be exhausted first).
existing_agents: Eteplirsen / golodirsen / viltolarsen / casimersen (approved single-exon PMOs — chemistry and regulatory precedent only, not applicable to this genotype)
WVE-N531 (stereopure exon-53 oligonucleotide, Phase 1/2, NCT04906460; OLE NCT07209332)
BMN 351 (exon-51 oligonucleotide, Phase 1/2, NCT06280209; OLE NCT07573631)
Exon 45-55 PMO cocktail in mdx52 mice (preclinical tool, PMID 30171548)
disease_relevant_cells: cardiomyocytes — required to prevent the dominant cause of death
satellite cells — not durably corrected by ASOs
CNS neurons (Dp427c/Dp140) — not addressable by systemic ASO

delivery_feasibility.target_tissue: All skeletal muscle plus myocardium; diaphragm is disproportionately important for survival
delivery_feasibility.target_cell: Myofiber nuclei (hundreds per fiber, all of which must be corrected to raise fiber-level dystrophin) and cardiomyocyte nuclei
delivery_feasibility.expected_access: Naked PMO: demonstrable but low — approved single-exon PMOs yield only low single-digit percent dystrophin in muscle with unclear functional benefit (PMID 28398005), and cardiac uptake is negligible, so the heart phenotype is untouched. A multi-ASO cocktail inherits this ceiling and then pays a multiplicative penalty because all ~11 oligos must co-occupy the same nascent transcript in the same nucleus. Peptide-conjugated PMO is the delivery technology that would be required; its clinical maturity is low and the most advanced DMD example (PGN-EDO51) was discontinued by its sponsor (NCT06079736, NCT06833931) (EVIDENCE). Antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates against TfR1 for muscle are earlier still and have no DMD efficacy readout I retrieved.
delivery_feasibility.major_constraint: Satellite cells are not corrected, so every regeneration cycle dilutes the effect and dosing must be lifelong and weekly-to-monthly; combined with the multiplicative cocktail penalty and near-zero cardiac delivery, the achievable fiber-level in-frame transcript fraction is the binding constraint.

supporting_evidence.statement: Systemic PMO cocktail-induced exon 45-55 skipping is an established, evaluable in vivo protocol in mdx52 mice with measurable dystrophin restoration — the geometry is experimentally real, not only theoretical.
The 45-55 multi-exon skip is systematically analysed as a broad-applicability strategy covering a large share of DMD mutations, so investment would serve a cohort far larger than this one patient.

The 45-55-deleted dystrophin protein is expressed and detectable in DMD patient-derived iPSCs across three distinct mutations, and naturally occurring del45-55 carriers have mild Becker phenotypes — the product is credible as functional.
Exon 55 lies inside the frame-neutral 45-55 block, so this skip removes the mutated exon while preserving the C-terminal anchoring domains that an exon-55 PTC otherwise abolishes.
Repeat chronic IV dosing of oligonucleotides in DMD children is procedurally and regulatorily established across several programs.

contradictory_evidence.statement: Approved exon-skipping ASOs achieve only low single-digit percent dystrophin with unclear functional benefit; muscle and heart delivery remain the limiting factor for naked PMO chemistry, and a multi-skip would plausibly perform worse per transcript.

Suvodirsen was terminated for lack of efficacy in a Phase 2/3 trial, demonstrating that improved oligonucleotide chemistry alone has not solved the DMD muscle-delivery problem even for a single-exon skip.

The peptide-conjugated DMD oligonucleotide most likely to enable multi-skip delivery, PGN-EDO51, was terminated/withdrawn by its sponsor, weakening the near-term delivery precedent this hypothesis depends on.

No clinical multi-exon-skip ASO exists in any indication; an 11-component cocktail is an unprecedented CMC and regulatory object (11 oligos, each needing its own impurity and toxicology package, plus combination justification).
ASOs do not correct satellite cells, so the effect is diluted by each necrosis-regeneration cycle and cannot be durable without indefinite redosing.

assessments.biggest_unknown: The fraction of transcripts that actually become fully 45-55-skipped at an achievable in vivo muscle concentration. Every ASO in the cocktail must engage the same pre-mRNA; if co-occupancy is the rate-limiting step the yield could be orders of magnitude below the already-marginal single-exon benchmark. Second unknown: whether a smaller frame-neutral block containing exon 55 exists for this patient's transcript.
assessments.biggest_failure_mode: Multiplicative cocktail inefficiency on top of an already-marginal muscle delivery ceiling: the program produces detectable but sub-therapeutic 45-55-skipped transcript in skeletal muscle and essentially none in heart, so the dilated cardiomyopathy that kills the patient progresses unchanged while the trial reads out on an ambulatory endpoint.
assessments.conclusion_note: The splicing mechanism and the functionality of the del45-55 protein product are well supported; what is uncertain is whether the required multiplicative skipping efficiency is physically achievable with any current chemistry. Recommended gating experiments, cheapest first: (1) compute from the patient's transcript whether a smaller frame-neutral block containing exon 55 exists; (2) titrate the cocktail in patient-derived myotubes and quantify fully-skipped transcript fraction by long-read sequencing, not by nested PCR which overstates minor products; (3) only if fiber-level dystrophin exceeds a prespecified threshold, pursue peptide-conjugated chemistry with explicit cardiac uptake endpoints. If step 2 yields sub-percent fully-skipped transcript, de-prioritise in favour of the readthrough route.
